grades.reason: Covers fork/exec behavior and process IDs. It says nothing about pipes, closing pipe ends, or EOF.
Covers lock-based parallelism in xv6. It mentions per-pipe locks but not EOF, closing the write end, or why a reader would block after a child exits.
Exercises on pipelines and dining philosophers deadlock. It does not explain why a pipe read fails to reach EOF.

grades.quote: The pipe code sleeps inside a loop checking the sleep condition; if there are multiple readers or writers, all but the first process to wake up will see the condition is false and sleep again.
grades.reason: Describes how xv6 piperead and pipewrite block and wake via sleep/wakeup, including a reader waiting on an empty buffer. It never mentions EOF, the writer-open condition, or closing unused write ends, which is the usual cause of the symptom. It is only loosely related background on reader blocking.
